parts.text: What diagnostic test will give a result within 24 hours?

parts_raw.text: What diagnostic test will give result within 24 hrs?

questions.model_answer: a) Reverse-transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR), ideally as a multiplex respiratory viral panel on a nasopharyngeal swab/wash; it is more sensitive than rapid antigen testing and returns results the same day. b) (1) RSV; (2) Influenza virus; (3) Parainfluenza virus; (4) Rhinovirus; (5) Human metapneumovirus; (6) Adenovirus (coronavirus is an acceptable sixth).

cohort_answer.text: Diagnostic test: RPP (respiratory pathogen panel). Viruses: Influenza; Rhinovirus; Parainfluenza; RSV; Human metapneumovirus; Adenovirus.

questions.question: RSV (Human Orthopneumovirus). What agent is used in the prevention of RSV in some patients? How does it work?

parts.text: What agent is used in the prevention of RSV in some patients? How does it work?

parts_raw.text: A.  What agent used in the prevention of RSV in some patients?  How does it work?

questions.model_answer: a) Palivizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody developed from a mouse monoclonal directed against a protective epitope of the RSV fusion (F) protein. It works by passive immunoprophylaxis: given IM at 15 mg/kg monthly (up to 5 doses) starting ~1 month before the RSV season, it supplies neutralizing anti-F antibody. It does not prevent RSV infection but decreases clinical severity, the risk of lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization in high-risk infants. (The newer agent nirsevimab is an extended half-life anti-prefusion-F monoclonal giving season-long protection from a single dose.)

cohort_answer.text:
Palivizumab. Passive immunoprophylaxis. Humanized monoclonal antibody. Target - RSV fusion (F) glycoprotein (protein found on the RSV). Does not interfere with response to routine immunizations to live virus vaccines (MMRV for ex). Indications: high risk infants/children: specifically shown to prevent severe RSV infection in kids with prematurity, BPD (bronchopulmonary dysplasia) and Congenital Heart Disease. When deciding if to give it, also consider severity of RSV season, distance to care for severe resp illness.

Indications for Palivizumab use - CPS statement (no change to this from previous): Children with hemodynamically significant CHD or CLD (defined as a need for oxygen at 36 weeks' GA) who require ongoing diuretics, bronchodilators, steroids or supplemental oxygen, should receive palivizumab if they are <12 months of age at the start of RSV season. In preterm infants without CLD born before 30 + 0 weeks' GA who are <6 months of age at the start of RSV season, it is reasonable (but not essential) to offer palivizumab. Infants in remote communities who would require air transportation for hospitalization born before 36 + 0 weeks' GA and <6 months of age at the start of RSV season should be offered palivizumab. Children with immunodeficiencies, Down syndrome, cystic fibrosis, upper airway obstruction or a chronic pulmonary disease other than CLD should not routinely be offered palivizumab. However, prophylaxis may be considered for children <24 months of age who are on home oxygen, have had a prolonged hospitalization for severe pulmonary disease or are severely immunocompromised.

parts.text: What agent is used in the prevention of RSV in some patients? How does it work?
In which patients is it indicated?
Name the two most common non-RSV causes of bronchiolitis in infants and children, with subtypes if appropriate.

parts_raw.text: A.  What agent used in the prevention of RSV in some patients?  How does it work?
In which patients is it indicated?
B.  Name the two most common non-RSV causes of bronchiolitis in infants and children with subtypes if appropriate.

questions.model_answer: a) Palivizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody directed against a protective epitope on the RSV fusion (F) glycoprotein. It provides passive immunoprophylaxis: given as 15 mg/kg IM monthly (up to 5 doses) beginning ~1 month before the RSV season, it neutralizes RSV and, although it does not prevent infection, it reduces clinical severity, lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization. b) High-risk infants in the first year of life: (1) prematurity (<29 weeks' gestation); (2) chronic (bronchopulmonary) lung disease; (3) hemodynamically/functionally significant congenital heart disease not surgically corrected; plus chronic conditions that impair handling of respiratory secretions (e.g., neuromuscular disease). In the second year it is reserved for preterm children with chronic lung disease still requiring oxygen/steroids/diuretics. c) (1) Rhinovirus; (2) Human parainfluenza virus (especially type 3); human metapneumovirus is the other frequently cited agent.
questions.beyond_mandell: Mandell lists rhinovirus, adenovirus, coronavirus, parainfluenza, human metapneumovirus and bocavirus as RSV co-infecting viruses but does not rank the leading non-RSV bronchiolitis causes; rhinovirus, parainfluenza type 3 and hMPV are the standard answers.

cohort_answer.text:
Passive immunization with palivizumab – monoclonal immunoglobulin against an epitope on the F glycoprotein of RSV.
Rhinovirus; Parainfluenza type 3; Human metapneumo virus

questions.question: RSV infection in a bone marrow (hematopoietic cell) transplant patient. Outline the management.
questions.model_answer: a) (1) Antiviral therapy with ribavirin — inhaled/aerosolized (2 g over 2-3 h TID intermittently, or 6 g over 18 h continuously) or oral/IV ribavirin, most effective when started while disease is still limited to the upper respiratory tract to prevent progression to lower tract disease; guard against teratogenicity. (2) Adjunctive immunoglobulin (IVIG) or anti-F monoclonal antibody (palivizumab) may be added in highly immunocompromised patients, though evidence is retrospective. (3) Supportive care (oxygen, hydration, respiratory support) plus strict infection-control/isolation to prevent nosocomial spread, with early diagnosis and screening on transplant units.

cohort_answer.text: Oral Ribavirin 15-20mg/kg/day divided TID x10 days; toxicities include teratogenicity (long t1/2), hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, cough/dyspnea/bronchoconstriction, neuropsychologic symptoms; can also consider IVIG and palivizumab.
